descriptionChirho: The concrete, literal sense of a puff of breath, mist, or vapor — something insubstantial that quickly dissipates, used as an image of transience and weightlessness.
The abstract, philosophical sense dominant in Ecclesiastes: the fundamental futility, meaninglessness, or absurdity of human endeavor and earthly existence under the sun.
Plural form denoting idol worship or false gods — the worthless, empty objects of pagan devotion that provoke the Lord to jealousy, characteristic of Deuteronomistic and prophetic usage.
